summary.headline: TBO TEK Q1 FY27: EBITDA-to-GTV of 1.3% and operating leverage shown despite Middle East disruption; 24% Europe growth, 15% organic CC growth.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) as the toughest in two years due to Middle East-driven travel disruption, yet reported top-line and bottom-line growth. Europe grew 24% YoY and Middle East was flat (1% CC growth), with Classic Vacations (acquired about six months ago) adding North America scale. EBITDA margins expanded faster than gross profit, which management cited as evidence of operating leverage. Management began reporting constant-currency numbers because a roughly 11% INR-vs-CC gap in hotel GTV distorted YoY growth. Management declined to give a timeline for Middle East normalisation or a long-term margin target.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Grew 24% YoY in a weak quarter, helped by market development investments made last year; management says Europe and APAC lead growth.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Analyst cited about 15% growth in APAC alongside 30%+ Europe; management said APAC and Europe are leading the growth charter.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Flat, +1% in constant currency; inbound travel to Middle East is under serious stress, while TBO's outbound business is less exposed.

segments.name: North America (Classic Vacations)
segments.commentary: North America is nearly a quarter of hotel GTV after Classic acquisition; Classic has highest GP profile (about 11%) and is seasonally strongest in Q1 on check-in basis.

segments.name: Airlines
segments.commentary: Airline GTV grew about 15% YoY; airline GP profile is about 1%, so airline mix shifts take rate.

guidance_outlook: Management aims for both QoQ and YoY growth; Q2 expected to be somewhat better than Q1 given July is the heaviest northern hemisphere travel month.
Management expects SG&A growth to be significantly slower than GP growth, though SG&A growth may tick up in Q2 due to increment season and opportunistic market development.
Classic platform integration expected to finish by end of calendar 2026; Classic-to-TBO selling expected to start early next year after platform migration.
Management said margins should expand as top-line normalises, but gave no long-term margin target; said it is not anchoring to 45-60% steady-state platform margins.
Operating leverage expected to continue; Q2 expected to show some margin expansion, Q3 historically lower revenue and margin dip.
Full-year Classic EBITDA margin of about 2.5% described as a fair assessment by management.
capex_capacity: Classic Vacations integration: North America feet-on-street sales hiring largely complete; enterprise CRM being implemented at Classic.
Platform integration (TBO and Classic) expected to be completed by calendar year end 2026.
VOYA AI itinerary tool is experimental; capex minimal and capitalised as intangibles; built in-house by tech team.
AI-based CRM layer launched a few weeks before the call; too early for results.
demand_pricing: Middle East situation described as extremely fluid; management declined to forecast when Middle East returns to growth.
Take rate slightly lower in Q1 as regions fought for business in the crisis; management accepted lower margins to win share.
Airfares very high; Middle East carriers disruption hit East-West travel, affecting India and Europe.
Management claims share gains in APAC and Europe, citing high double-digit growth in a market with no organic growth.
GTV split between retail and B2B/API roughly 50-50, unchanged from last quarter; management will review disclosure.
Management expects bigger players to gain share as smaller and mid-sized players attrite post crisis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1.3% consolidated EBITDA-to-GTV sustainable and can it grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA-to-GTV is tricky due to airline vs hotel take-rate differences; the right metric is EBITDA-to-GP, at about 26%, which should keep improving.

qa_highlights.question: How should organic growth be modelled once conditions normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a return to the growth profile of Q3 FY26, timing uncertain (Q3 or Q4); Europe and APAC lead, with North America growth expected from October-December on a like-for-like basis.

qa_highlights.question: How will Classic's December-quarter consolidation affect GP growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two opposing forces exist: Classic has not yet delivered standalone enterprise growth (a few quarters away), while pre-war organic growth in Jan-Feb was above 15%.

qa_highlights.question: How long can APAC and Europe growth last before the next investment cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: A key account manager typically shows four to six quarters of growth; no early signs of slowdown, with investments expected to be sticky.

qa_highlights.question: Is the SG&A run-rate of about 4% sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SG&A growth may expand a little in the short term due to increment season and market development, but will be range-bound and slower than top line.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 30 bps drop in organic hotels GP/GTV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not split the drop between lower Middle East saliency and deliberate margin cuts to protect volumes, saying both occurred.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net cash position and cross-sell status?
qa_highlights.answer: Cash in bank Rs. 1,980+ crore against USD 70 million loan and EUR 6 million working capital loan; about INR 65 crore of TBO-to-Classic sales, reverse flow not yet started.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 11% currency impact due to a policy change?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no policy change; the gap is purely rupee depreciation, and CC reporting will continue directionally.
